background.executionContext:
**Commands used:** `goto`, `htmlsnapshot`, `htmlsnapshot get`, `htmlsnapshot query`, `eval`, `crawl`, `swarm create`, `swarm query`, `swarm status`, `swarm result`, `loop`, `session-default`, `list`, `tab-list`, `status`

**Workarounds required:** `session-default` for loop flag passing, `DOM_FIRST_ATTR` instead of `DOM_FIRST_HREF`, 12-minute Maven build for MockSite

---
background.task:
The task covered all six branches of SKILL.md §4b. Four of six acceptance criteria succeeded; two failed due to product/reliability issues.

| AC | Description | Status |
|----|-------------|--------|
| AC1 | Single list page via `htmlsnapshot query` | ✅ Success |
| AC2 | Multiple known URLs via `crawl --seed-file` | ✅ Success |
| AC3 | Crawl from start URL with link discovery | ❌ Failed |
| AC4 | Parallel execution with swarm | ❌ Failed |
| AC5 | Repeated monitoring with loop | ✅ Success (workaround) |
| AC6 | Few URLs in shell script | ✅ Success |

### AC1 — Single list page: ✅ SUCCESS
- Navigated to MockSite listing page, discovered `.product-card`, `.product-title`, `.product-price` selectors
- X-SQL query with `DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, '.product-card')` returned 6 product rows with correlated fields
- Minor issue: `DOM_FIRST_HREF` returned empty; `DOM_FIRST_ATTR(DOM, '.product-link', 'href')` worked

### AC2 — Multiple known URLs via seed file: ✅ SUCCESS
- Crawl extracted 3 rows (url, title, price) from 3 MockSite product detail pages
- Took 428 seconds for 3 lightweight local pages

### AC3 — Crawl with link discovery: ❌ FAILED
- Crawl hub page loads in browser and `a.product` elements exist (confirmed via eval)
- Crawl's page-loader (non-JS HTTP fetch) does NOT see `.product` class — diagnostic: "The page has 12 anchors but `a.product` matched zero elements"
- Same issue confirmed with `htmlsnapshot query` via scrape API

### AC4 — Swarm parallel execution: ❌ FAILED
- Worker pool consistently stalls: 1/3 jobs completed first attempt, 0/3 second attempt
- `--wait` flag timed out at 300s with no completions

### AC5 — Loop monitoring: ✅ SUCCESS (with workaround)
- Loop subcommand cannot pass `-s <name>` through `--` separator
- Workaround: `session-default` to set target session, then loop works correctly

### AC6 — Shell loop: ✅ SUCCESS
- Bash loop iterated over 3 URLs, extracting title + price correctly

---

issues.title: Swarm worker pool stalls — jobs stuck as 'queued' indefinitely

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: 1. swarm create --display-mode HEADLESS. 2. swarm query --sql @q.sql --seed-file urls.txt --refresh. 3. Observe 1/3 complete, 2 stuck. 4. Clear, recreate, resubmit. 5. 0/3 complete, all stuck for 300+s.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: All swarm jobs should be picked up by workers and complete within a reasonable time.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: First attempt: 1/3 completed, 2 stuck. Second attempt: 0/3 completed, all stuck. --wait timed out at 300s.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The swarm worker pool appears to have a race condition or initialization failure. The worker pool may depend on session state that was corrupted, or headless browser contexts may fail to initialize silently.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add health-check endpoint for swarm worker pool status
- Surface worker initialization errors in swarm status output
- Add automatic worker restart on stall detection
- Add a --timeout-per-job flag instead of only the global --wait timeout

issues.title: Task instruction uses $(./b4w.ps1) invocation that does not work in bash

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: On Linux/bash, follow task instruction to use $(./b4w.ps1) goto <url>. The $(...) is command substitution in bash, not invocation.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Either the task should specify the correct Linux invocation (./b4w.sh) or the wrapper scripts should be unified across platforms.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: SKILL.md §Invocation explicitly warns: 'The $(./b4w.ps1) <command> syntax shown in some task instructions does NOT work in bash — $(…) is command substitution, not invocation.' Yet the task instructions mandate this exact syntax.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The task template hardcodes a Windows/PowerShell-specific invocation pattern that is incompatible with Linux/bash. The SKILL.md documentation correctly identifies this issue but the task instructions contradict it.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Update task templates to use platform-appropriate invocation (./b4w.sh on Linux, ./b4w.ps1 on Windows)
- Add a wrapper that auto-detects platform and selects the right script
- Consider a single ./b4w entry point that works cross-platform

issues.title: Crawl execution is extremely slow — 428s for 3 URLs, 600s timeout for link discovery

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run crawl --seed-file urls.txt --depth 0 --sql @query.sql with 3 local MockSite URLs. Observe a 428-second runtime. Run crawl with link discovery (-d 1 or 2) and observe 600s timeout.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Crawling 3 lightweight local pages should complete in under 30 seconds.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: 3 local URLs took 428 seconds (2+ minutes per page). Link discovery crawl timed out at 600 seconds while still waiting for the first page.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The crawl mechanism appears to use a full browser page load with extensive waiting. The 'waiting for first page' polling message suggests the page load is stalling or the load-detection heuristic is too conservative.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Reduce default page load timeout for simple static pages
- Add a 'fast mode' for local/static pages that skips heavy load detection
- Profile the page load pipeline to identify the bottleneck
- Consider using the scrape API (SimpleHttpFetcher) for depth-0 bulk fetches

issues.title: Crawl link discovery cannot see JavaScript-added CSS classes

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: 1. Open crawl hub in browser — eval confirms a.product elements exist. 2. Run crawl with -ol a.product — diagnostic: 'The page has 12 anchors but a.product matched zero elements.'

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Link discovery should work with the same selectors that work in the browser DOM.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The crawl's page-loading mechanism produces different HTML than the browser DOM. JavaScript-added CSS classes are invisible. X-SQL DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT confirmed same issue.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The crawl uses a non-JS HTTP fetch that captures server-rendered HTML without executing JavaScript. Client-side class additions are invisible. This is a fundamental architectural gap.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Document clearly that crawl link selectors must match server-rendered HTML, not JS-modified DOM
- Add a --browser-links flag to extract links from the live browser DOM
- Update the diagnostic to mention this JS vs static HTML distinction
- Consider a 'crawl inspect' command that shows what the crawl fetcher sees

issues.title: MockSite requires undocumented 12+ minute Maven local build prerequisite

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run ./bin/test.ps1 mock-site from a fresh checkout. It fails because browser4-rest and pulsar-tests-common JARs are not in local Maven repo. Requires ./mvnw install -pl browser4-rest -am -DskipTests (12+ minutes).

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The task should document that MockSite depends on local Maven artifacts that must be built first, or provide a one-command setup step.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: MockSite failed to start with dependency resolution errors. Required a 12-minute multi-module Maven build before MockSite could launch.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: MockSite's Maven POM depends on sibling modules (browser4-rest, pulsar-tests-common) that aren't published to Maven Central. They must be mvn installed locally first.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a setup step to the task: './mvnw install -pl browser4-rest -am -DskipTests && pwsh ./bin/test.ps1 mock-site'
- Document expected build time (~12 minutes) in task prerequisites
- Consider pre-building these artifacts in CI to eliminate this step

issues.title: Loop subcommand cannot pass -s <session> flag through -- separator

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.sh loop --name test --count 2 -i 10 -- -s price-watch eval 'document.title'. Observe: 'Error: Unknown command: price-watch'

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The -s price-watch should be passed as arguments to the nested browser4-cli process.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The nested CLI interprets 'price-watch' as a command name. Argument parsing after -- drops flag-value association.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The argument tokenization after -- splits -s and price-watch into separate tokens that are passed independently. The nested CLI sees 'price-watch' as a positional argument.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/loop.rs — function that assembles subcommand arguments for the nested browser4-cli process

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Fix argument assembly to preserve flag-value pairs
- Add a test case for loop subcommand with -s flag
- Document the known limitation in loop.md
- Consider adding --session-name as a loop-level flag

issues.title: session-default with swarm interaction causes session loss

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: 1. swarm create. 2. session-default price-watch. 3. swarm close. 4. list — shows 'No active browser sessions' even though price-watch session should still exist.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Closing the swarm session should not affect other named sessions.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: After swarm close + session-default changes, all sessions disappeared. The price-watch named session was lost.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Session lifecycle management has an interaction between session-default, swarm create (which sets default to SWARM), and swarm close.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add session isolation guarantees — closing one session should never affect others
- Document the interaction between session-default and swarm session management
- Add a warning when session-default is about to overwrite an existing default

issues.title: Commands compile on every invocation making shell scripts slow

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run the AC6 shell loop script. Each ./b4w.sh invocation recompiles the Rust binary, adding ~0.5s per command. A 3-URL loop with 4 commands per URL adds ~6s of overhead.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The binary should be compiled once and reused across invocations.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Each ./b4w.sh invocation independently runs cargo, adding noticeable compilation overhead in scripts.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The ./b4w.sh script uses cargo run which has per-invocation overhead. No persistent dev server mode.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: b4w.sh

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Build the binary once with cargo build and use the artifact directly
- Implement a daemon mode where the CLI stays resident

issues.title: DOM_FIRST_HREF returns empty while DOM_FIRST_ATTR with 'href' works

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: In X-SQL query scoped to .product-card, DOM_FIRST_HREF(DOM, '.product-link') returns empty. DOM_FIRST_ATTR(DOM, '.product-link', 'href') returns correct relative URL.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: DOM_FIRST_HREF should return the href attribute value.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: DOM_FIRST_HREF returned empty for all 6 product cards. DOM_FIRST_ATTR works correctly.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: DOM_FIRST_HREF may use a different DOM traversal or attribute resolution strategy than DOM_FIRST_ATTR. The scoped DOM context may affect how href resolution works.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Investigate the implementation difference between DOM_FIRST_HREF and DOM_FIRST_ATTR for href
- Add a test case for DOM_FIRST_HREF with scoped DOM and relative URLs
- Document any known limitations in x-sql.md

issues.title: htmlsnapshot capture HTTP timeout at 60s is too short and --timeout flag doesn't affect it

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot (after stale session). Observe 'HTTP request timed out [tool=html_snapshot_capture, timeout=60s]'. Using --timeout 120 does not change the 60s value.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The global --timeout flag should override the default 60s tool timeout.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Capture timed out at exactly 60 seconds. Passing --timeout 120 did not change the timeout value in the error message.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The HTTP client timeout for MCP tool calls appears to be separate from the --timeout global flag.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Make --timeout flag override the MCP HTTP request timeout
- Increase default htmlsnapshot capture timeout to 120s
- Document which timeouts --timeout affects

issues.title: Constant Rust compilation overhead on every command invocation (~0.5s)

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run any ./b4w.sh command. Observe 'Compiling browser4-cli ... Finished dev profile in 0.XXs' before every command.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: In dev mode, the binary should be compiled once and reused, or a daemon mode should be available.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Every command invocation recompiles the Rust binary (~0.4-0.6s).

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The ./b4w.sh wrapper uses cargo run which has per-invocation overhead.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: b4w.sh — the cargo run invocation

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Build the binary once with cargo build and use the artifact directly in dev mode
- Add a 'dev install' command that builds and symlinks the binary

issues.title: dead_code compiler warning clutters every command output

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run any ./b4w.sh command. Observe: 'warning: constant QUICK_START_COMMANDS is never used --> src/help.rs:83:7'

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Compiler warnings should be suppressed in normal operation.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Every command output includes a 7-line Rust compiler warning about an unused constant.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: QUICK_START_COMMANDS in src/help.rs is defined but never referenced.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs:83 — QUICK_START_COMMANDS constant

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Either use the QUICK_START_COMMANDS constant or remove it
- Add #[allow(dead_code)] attribute
- Consider cargo build --quiet in the wrapper script
